abstract: Exploiting the high repetition rate of a monolithically integrated, fiber-coupled and mode-locked laser diode, we were able to accurately reconstruct the time axis of a compact terahertz time-domain spectroscopy (THz-TDS) system without an interferometer or a delay-line encoder. We achieved acquisition rates of 0.5 traces per second using a continuous driving mode of the optical delay unit (ODU) while maintaining a precise time.

articleTitle: THz Fourier Imaging Based on Sub-harmonic Heterodyne Detection
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A high-resolution THz imaging system based on the coherent recording of the Fourier space spectrum by sub-har-monic heterodyne detection is described. The 600-GHz imaging wave and the 300-GHz reference wave, locked to each other with a slight frequency offset, are received by a broad-band Si CMOS TeraFET mixer. The complex-valued Fourier space spectrum is recorded in the focal plane of the imaging system in raster-scanning mode, after which the imaged scene is reconstructed by inverse Fourier transformation. This allows the system to work in the virtual imaging regime and brings the theoretical resolution limit of the system to the level of half the imaging wavelength.

articleTitle: Molecular Organization of Water at the Hydrophilic Silica/Liquid Interface Probed by Sum Frequency Generation Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We Investigate the orientation and structuring of strong protic solvents as a model system for separation techniques. Hydrophilic interaction liquid chromatography (HILIC) is an alternative mode to high performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) for separating highly polar and amphiphilic analytes. However, inconsistency of retention mechanism contributions has limited the advancement of the separation technique. The consensus is that both the liquid/liquid and solid/liquid interfaces may play a vital role in shedding light to these contributions. Knowing the specific molecular organization near surfaces may pave way to understanding the functional role of the liquid solvent mixture adsorbed at the interface. Surface selective vibrational sum-frequency generation (VSFG) is a second order ultrafast spectroscopic technique suitable for such studies, where the interfacial layers are selectively probed. We present here spectroscopic measurements of a double-layer formation of liquid methanol at the interface as well as probing the interfacial organization of water at the hydrophilic silica/liquid interface. Measurements of the methyl region of liquid methanol on hydrophilic surfaces have remained elusive, but here we report the first observation on the CH stretch spectrum.

articleTitle: THz Time-Domain Characterization of Amplifying Quantum-Cascade Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present direct measurements using reflection-mode terahertz (THz) time domain spectroscopy (TDS) of amplifying quantum-cascade (QC) metasurfaces used in THz QC-VECSELs. Devices resonant at 2.2 and 2.5 THz are studied under different bias currents, and exhibit gain-induced partial compensation of losses.

articleTitle: Gapless Sensitive Detection of Ultrabroadband Infrared Pulses Using Single Crystal of Diamond
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate the coherent detection of ultrabroadband infrared pulses generated from two-color pumped air plasma in a wide spectral range using single crystal of diamond as a medium for field induced second harmonic generation.

articleTitle: Development of terahertz optical sources for an excitation wavelength of 1.56 μm
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Herein, we develop optical sources for the generation of high-intensity terahertz pulses utilizing the heterostructure-mediated photo-Dember effect. In particular, InAs/GaSb/InAs heterostructures that can be operated with an excitation wavelength of 1.56 μm were examined. In order to increase the carrier absorption in the GaSb injection layer, we introduced an InGaSb layer. Increased terahertz radiation was obtained owing to the increased absorption of the InGaSb injection layer.

articleTitle: Metasurface Broadband Polarization Converters Towards Terahertz Circular Dichroism Spectroscopy

articleTitle: Investigation of THz imaging artifacts generated by oversampling and interpolation of diffraction-limited low-resolution data
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work, we investigate artifacts that can be generated during the post-processing of THz imaging data using spatial oversampling and interpolation - as often applied to artificially increase the impression of spatial resolution. We also present Terahertz (THz) near-field measurements with subwavelength resolution and compare them to diffraction-limited far-field measurements.

articleTitle: THz Superradiant Emission from 1550-nm Pulse-Pumped Quantum-Dot Arrays
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a study on the generation of THz radiation with quantum dot arrays by utilizing their cooperative superradiant behavior when driven resonantly by a ~100 fs laser pulse.

articleTitle: Dynamic THz signatures of charge-lattice correlations
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The hybrid metal halide perovskites have shown enormous promise for optoelectronic devices, including efficient photovoltaics, however their insensitivity to defects has remained puzzling. Polaron correlations have been cited as a possible means to protect charge carriers from defect scattering. In this paper, we show time-resolved THz spectroscopy measurements are capable of directly probing polaron correlations via an intra-band coherent beat arising from center-of-mass quasi-particle motion and the internal motion of charge within its self-induced potential. We describe these measurements indicating that charge carriers do indeed exist as polarons, which are coherent for several hundred femtoseconds following photon absorption.

articleTitle: Quantifying Nail Varnish Drying Using a THz Vector Network Analyser
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Nail varnish and its drying properties are explored in detail using a terahertz vector network analyser in a quasioptical transmission configuration. Assessing the `dryness' of nail varnish through the measurement of transmitted terahertz radiation, as opposed to qualitative, and typically touch-based techniques, takes into account the non-uniform drying of the nail varnish as a function of its depth. This method can be used to assess the actual dryness of the layer overall and offer measurable parameters to quantify the drying properties of each mixture.

articleTitle: Cell Culture Confluency as a Potential Factor in Biological Effects of Millimetre Wave Radiation in In Vitro Experiments
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In in vitro experiments and related numerical simulations, dedicated to determine the incident power and energy absorbed, cell monolayer is considered to be thin and homogeneous, although in reality this is rarely the case. In this study, we consider cell culture confluency as a factor of the layer non-uniformity and the effect of this factor on electromagnetic field distribution within the cell layer. Results of simple case simulation demonstrated significant field concentration on the cell membrane as well as fast and dynamic temperature gradients.

articleTitle: Effect of Millimeter Waves on Genome Architecture and the Transcriptome of Primary Human Fibroblasts
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Millimeter waves (MMWs) are known to induce a range of biological effects, although the causes remain largely unknown. We exposed primary human fibroblasts to MMWs and observed changes in the genome architecture, with modified DNA secondary structure formation effecting gene expression and subsequent protein production. This work establishes the potential for MMWs to induce targeted modifications to the chromatin landscape for therapeutic applications.

articleTitle: MHz-repetition rate THz sources with high average power
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present recent advances in the demonstration of THz-TDS setups combining high average power of tens of milliwatts with high repetition rate in the Megahertz regime, based on laser excitation using >100W class ultrafast laser drivers.

articleTitle: 2D - THz-Spectroscopy on a Quantum Cascade Structure
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We use two-dimensional (2D) THz-spectroscopy to study the χ<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(3)</sup> non-linearities originating from four-wave mixing (FWM) in a quantum cascade structure (QCS), embedded in a single-plasmon waveguide. This approach allows us to extract the strength of all system non-linearities, study time-resolved system properties such as population and coherence lifetimes, as well as identify the dominant scattering mechanisms of the unbiased QCS at 10K.

articleTitle: Terahertz emission amplitude-based 2D mapping of the Fe thickness profile in Fe/Pt spintronic heterostructure
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate the feasibility of mapping metallic layer thickness profile in 2 dimension based on the amplitude of the terahertz emission of a large area spintronic heterostructure. A Fe/Pt bilayer was deposited on glass substrate such that a 100 mm diameter circular space was covered with 4 nm Pt throughout and with a gradient of 0.5 nm to 7 nm thick Fe by magnetron sputtering. The Fe thickness dependence of the spintronic THz emission is clearly observed in just one sample by two-dimensional amplitude mapping.

articleTitle: Inverse Designed Flat Optics for Imaging Applications in the IR and beyond
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Treating phase in the image plane to be a free parameter, we demonstrate multilevel diffractive lenses via inverse design enabling functionalities like achromaticity, depth-of-focus, wide-angle imaging, etc. for various imaging applications in the IR and beyond.

articleTitle: High-speed, low-noise thermoelectric graphene detectors at terahertz frequencies
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report room temperature terahertz detection in hBN/graphene/hBN heterostructures, integrated in top-gated field effect transistors. The record combination of high-speed (response time <; 1 ns) and high sensitivity (noise equivalent power ~ 100 pWHz-1I2) is enabled by the photo-thermoelectric effect and paves the way for the design of ultrafast graphene arrays in the far infrared, opening concrete perspectives for targeting ultrafast applications.

articleTitle: Excitons in twisted van der Waals bilayers: Internal structure and ultrafast dynamics
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: By probing internal 1s-2p transitions with phase-locked mid-infrared pulses, we reveal the internal structure and binding energy of photo-generated excitons in transition metal dichalcogenide bilayers. Furthermore, we trace how the twist angle precisely controls the ultrafast formation of interlayer excitons and tunes excitonic hybridization in hetero- and homobilayers, respectively.

articleTitle: Broadband Anti-Reflection Moth-Eye Structures Realized in the Above 1 THz Region by Laser Processing
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We fabricate terahertz (THz) moth-eye antireflection (AR) structures on the surface of high-resistivity silicon via low-power femtosecond laser processing. We observed broadband AR performance at near-unity above 0.8 THz, where the upper value was measurement limited. Such values are unprecedented for laser fabricated samples, and shows the high potential of laser processing-based approaches for THz optics fabrication.

articleTitle: High-Risk Factor Detection of Coronary Artery Disease by Terahertz Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Methylglyoxal (MGO) is an important high-risk factor of coronary artery disease. While the existing detection methods for MGO are time-consuming and high-cost. Here we demonstrate that the terahertz spectroscopy can be used to qualitatively identify the abnormally high concentration of MGO and quantitatively analysis the normal MGO blood concentration.

articleTitle: Direct Spectroscopic Imaging of Medicine Tablets using Monochromatic Tunable Terahertz-wave Source and Highly Sensitive Semiconductor Detector
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We investigated direct spectroscopic imaging of just opened, unformed over the counter (OTC) medicine tablets using a monochromatic tunable pulsed THz-wave source and highly sensitive semiconductor detector. This simple transmission power spectroscopic measurement does not need any complex post process to obtain images. We acquired transmission images of OTC medicine tablets and compared with the images obtained by a commercial THz-TDS system.

articleTitle: Terahertz Imaging for Topical and Micro/Nano Needle Patch Drug Delivery
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate the ability of THz imaging to evaluate the efficacy of transdermal drug delivery. Effects of transdermal drug delivery by topical and micro/nano-needle patch methods are measured. Our results prove that THz imaging is able to monitor the improved drug delivery efficacy given by a nanoneedle patch.

articleTitle: Design of a quasioptical test bench for VNA extenders
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The CAD design, simulated optical performance, and test measurements of a quasioptical test bench for VNA extenders are presented. The system allows straightforward integration of off axis parabolic mirrors and VNA extenders. The mirror orientation reduces aberrations and results suggest optical properties are close to what is expected with geometric ray tracing.

articleTitle: Photo-carrier doping effect on high-order harmonic generation in monolayer WSe2
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have investigated the photo-carrier doping effect on high-order harmonic generation in monolayer WSe<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. The intensity change of harmonics induced by the photo-carrier doping suggests that the interband and intraband mechanism is comparable in the lower energy region than the absorption edge whereas the interband mechanism is dominant in the higher energy region.

articleTitle: Post-processing GHz-level frequency tuning of THz Quantum Cascade Lasers
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Frequency red tuning down to GHz-level is shown in THz Quantum Cascade Lasers, by post-processing alteration of the device. Changing the height difference between the active region and surrounding material (and reapplying a material of known refractive index with appropriate thickness), the mode effective refractive index is increased, causing the device to lase at a lower frequency.

articleTitle: Two Wavelet-based Algorithms for Chemical Recognition Using Transmission Terahertz Spectral Imaging Through Turbid Media
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Dielectric heterogeneity in addition to wavelength-scale air voids and granular particles lead to significant electromagnetic scattering in the transmission-mode THz-TDS. These scattering processes result in the distorted or obscured resonant signatures, a frequency-dependent extinction loss, and the appearance of anomalous spectral artifacts, imposing severe challenges on the real-world automatic material characterization schemes. In this work, we use a combination of the wavelet multiresolution analysis, the principal component analysis, and the bimodality coefficient to simultaneously identify all the resonant frequencies of a heterogeneous sample embedded beneath a highly scattering turbid medium.

articleTitle: Carbon nanotubes metasurface integrated with silicon microfluidic channel for THz sensor
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A novel design for terahertz sensor based on carbon nanotubes (CNTs) metasurface and silicon metasurface integrated with microfluidic channel is proposed. Obvious enhanced resonant absorption peak observed are attributed to the coupling of the CNTs and silicon metasurfaces which excites the surface plasmon resonance. The peak absorbance is higher than 99% at the resonance frequencies with the higher quality factor (Q). The refractive index sensing capabilities of various solutions flowing into the sample cell through the microfluidic channel are also investigated. The results indicate that the proposed device can be used for sensing various materials with different refractive index.

articleTitle: Low cost and stable THz-TDS system using laser chaos
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Low cost and stable THz waves generation and detection are achieved using laser chaos. This system applied to THz spectroscopy to distinguish water and oil.

articleTitle: Near-field study of the strong coupling between intersubband transitions in quantum wells and single patch antenna resonators in the mid-infrared
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Exploiting the coupling of laser beams to atomic force microscopy probes, both scattering and absorption of mid-infrared radiation (wavelengths of 5 to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$11\ \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>) have been measured in the near field region of single patch-antennas, strongly coupled to the intersubband transition of an InGaAs/AlInAs quantum well.

articleTitle: Ultra-slow recombination of carriers at low density and energy in neutral graphene-hBN van der Waals heterostructures
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on carrier lifetimes in graphene/hBN heterostructures of ~30 ps for photoexcited carriers at low density and energy, using mid-infrared photoconductivity measurements. We further demonstrate the switching of carrier lifetime from ~30 ps (attributed to interband Auger) down to a few picoseconds upon ignition of hyperbolic phonon polaritons relaxation at finite bias and/or with infrared excitation power. Our study opens interesting perspectives to exploit graphene/hBN heterostructures for THz lasing and highly sensitive THz photodetection as well as for phonon polariton optics.

articleTitle: Parts-per-million water vapor sensing using an ultrahigh-Q THz disc microresonator
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report on the first demonstration of a THz gas spectrometer using a sub-wavelength thick ultrahigh-Q THz disc microresonator. Leveraging the microresonator's ultrahigh quality factor in excess of 120,000 and the intrinsically large evanescent field, allows for the implementation of a very compact spectrometer without the need for complex multi-pass gas cells. Water vapor concentrations as low as 4 parts per million at atmospheric conditions have been readily achieved in these proof-of-concept experiments.

articleTitle: Terahertz Spectroscopic Investigation into Cocrystal Formation Process within Lamivudine and Theophylline
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A novel pharmaceutical cocrystal of lamivudine and theophylline obtained through liquid assisted grinding (LAG) has been characterized by terahertz spectroscopic technique. Spectral results indicate that the fingerprint spectrum of the cocrystal is different from the raw parent materials. The dynamic process of such pharmaceutical cocrystal formation has also been monitored directly with THz spectra.

articleTitle: Extracting Anharmonic Coupling Constants from Beta-Barium Borate
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Multidimensional terahertz (THz) spectroscopy is a powerful tool for understanding nonlinear excitation, coherent energy flow, and coupling between collective degrees of freedom on ultrafast time scales. With extreme vibrational excitation using high-field THz light, 2D THz spectroscopy can reveal how anharmonic mode coupling results in coherent energy transfer. We explore phononic coupling between modes in β-barium borate and attempt to extract the coupling constants.

articleTitle: Cocrystal Formation between Isoniazid and Protocatechuic Acid Based on Terahertz Spectroscopy and DFT Simulation
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The cocrystal of isoniazid and protocatechuic acid under slow solvent evaporation condition has been characterized by terahertz spectroscopic technique. We used DFT to calculate the THz absorption spectrum of the cocrystal, which is consistent with the experimental results. And vibrational modes of the cocrystal between isoniazid and protocatechuic acid were assigned.

articleTitle: Investigation of 5-Fluorouracil Cocrystals by Low-Frequency Vibrational Spectroscopy and Solid-State Density Functional Theory
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Cocrystallization of dissimilar organic molecules plays an important role in the design and improvement of solid-state pharmaceuticals. The combined approach of terahertz and Raman spectroscopies, augmented with solid-state density functional theory, offers a powerful method for studying the distinct low-frequency vibrational spectra of these novel solids and the energetic factors involved in cocrystal formation. Here, 5-fluorouracil (a chemotherapy agent) and its 1:1 cocrystals with urea and thiourea are investigated. The first goal is to understand the two polymorphs of 5-fluorouracil and to accurately model the fluorine-fluorine interactions between molecules. In addition to pure 5-fluorouracil, the effects of sulfur and oxygen on the hydrogen bonding networks within the cocrystalline solids is also considered, and how these modify the low-frequency vibrations.

articleTitle: Terahertz physics of graphene: from linear conductivity to high-harmonics generation
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this tutorial we review the electronic bandstructure of graphene, identify its conductive properties stemming from the ultrarelativistic nature of its electrons, and discuss the thermodynamic picture of ultrafast electron transport in graphene. We will demonstrate that the collective thermodynamic response of background electrons leads to extreme high nonlinearity of graphene in the THz range, permitting very strong saturable absorption and extremely efficient THz high harmonics generation.

articleTitle: A THz-Driven Field Emission Electron Gun
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We are developing a high-gradient, THz-driven electron gun. THz-frequency accelerator structures can enable the development of compact, bright, and efficient particle sources. Our two cell standing-wave gun is powered by a 110 GHz gyrotron and will produce 350 keV electrons with 500 k W of input power. The field emission cathode is a copper tip located in the first cell. High power measurements will include diagnostics to measure the energy spread, charge, and size of the resulting bunch.

articleTitle: Object Detection without Line of Sight using Leaky THz Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate a 2D real-time object tracking system for the THz region using a leaky parallel-plate waveguide radar. Because the system is based on broadband excitation, it can locate multiple objects simultaneously, as well as objects for which there is no direct line-of-sight view.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Conversion Between Polarization States Based on Metasurface with Broadband Performance
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Dual-band operation for terahertz (THz) wireless systems to merge multiple systems into a single one is a challenging problem. We propose a dual-band THz polarization converter using metasurfaces in transmission modes. It is singly layered which makes it a very simple structure. Dual-band conversion from linear wave to circular wave is reported over 20% of centre frequencies (1.6-1.97 THz, 3.35-4.16 THz) which is very broadband. Idea is verified by simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: Unique Terahertz Features of Fentanyl and its Analogs Revealed via High Performance Computations
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Fentanyl is one of the most potent synthetic opioid pain relievers. However, the abuse of opioids may lead to death. Rapid identification methods of both known and emerging opioid substances in fentanyl family would help to prevent this abuse. Terahertz (THz) spectra provide the identification information without damaging the sample. In this study, we predict THz spectra of fentanyl and 20 of its analogs in solid state by density-functional theory method PBEh-3c to investigate the frequencies of rotational-vibrational normal modes in THz region (0.1~100 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>). Substitution of single bond or aromatic group of fentanyl leads to significant change of crystal packing and is reflected in its THz spectrum. We discuss structure-property relationships of these synthetic opioids such as ohmefentanyl and sufentanil that are more potent than fentanyl. Since new drugs come up in black market frequently, we applied machine learning methods to predict THz spectrum of yet unknown synthetic opioids. Other “white powders” such as sucrose and lactose will be tested to validate our prediction.

articleTitle: Non-contact inspection of Moisture Change Based on CW Terahertz Reflectometry
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a method for measuring water content in a sample using CW terahertz reflectometry. A Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) is used to irradiate a 300 GHz band terahertz wave to a wet sample, and the complex reflection coefficient is measured. The temporal change of the water content is thus observed by analyzing the change of the complex reflection coefficient. By fitting the measurement result with a multi-reflection model, we experimentally confirmed the observation of the moisture change on a paper sample.

articleTitle: Link Configuration Impact on High-Bandwidth Digital Signal Transmission in the 300 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The ever-increasing demand for bandwidth for mobile data transmission has led to the use of higher frequency bands. In addition to increasing bandwidth requirements, regulation in the classic frequency bands is also a reason for the “escape to the top”. In the present work, the influence of beam properties, distance and reflection as well as complexity of modulation on high bit-rate data transmission is investigated using an experimental 300 GHz transmission system in conjunction with a bit error rate test system.

articleTitle: Effect of Doped Buffer in Low-Temperature-Grown GaAs Terahertz Photoconductive Antenna Emitters and Detectors
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) photoconductive antenna (PCA) fabricated on low-temperature-grown GaAs (LT-GaAs) with layer structure consisting of a doped buffer exhibited enhanced THz emission for LT-GaAs grown at lower temperature. As THz emitter, the LT-GaAs grown at 270°C with doped buffer generated THz radiation with amplitude twice as that of its undoped counterpart. Similar effect is not observed when the LT-GaAs is grown at 320°C with doped buffer, which is expected to have higher THz emission. As THz detector, both LT-GaAs with doped buffer exhibited identical and improved detection sensitivity regardless of the LT-GaAs growth temperature.

articleTitle: Carrier Lifetime of Au-Hyperdoped Ge using Terahertz Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Gold-hyperdoped germanium extends the photodetection beyond the cut-off wavelength of germanium into the infrared wavelengths. Ion implantation followed by pulsed-laser melting process makes a single crystal material with ultrahigh dopant concentrations. The laser parameters influence the dopant's atomic position which leads to different light absorption and carrier transport properties. Time resolved terahertz spectroscopy is used to evaluate the charge carrier lifetime which gives an insight into the defect energetics and atomic location.

articleTitle: Terahertz Wave Generation from Water at Different Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We experimentally measure the temperature dependence of terahertz generation from a liquid water line excited by sub-picosecond laser pulses. To study the effect of water density change on THz wave emission, the water temperature range is set from 3.5 to 90 °C, with a smaller step between 3.5 and 5.5 °C due to the maximum density of liquid water at 4.0 °C. Moreover, the relationship between water flow rate and temperature is investigated. The result shows the measured change of emitted THz field vs the variation of water temperature.

articleTitle: Influence of photo-excited charge carriers in silicon wafer in a two-color laser-induced air plasma terahertz emission
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We demonstrate that the far-field terahertz beam generated from a Ti:Sapphire two-color laser-induced filament can exhibit a conical or a Gaussian distribution depending on the filtering experimental conditions. Using a 2D electro-optic detection, we provide the first clear evidence that the conical emission in the 0.2-2.6 THz spectral range is due to photo-induced carriers in the silicon filter typically used to block the remaining pump laser light. The low-frequency terahertz beam retrieves an almost Gaussian spatial distribution when the silicon filter is preceded by a large bandgap ceramic filter, which stops the pump beam, preventing carriers generation in the silicon filter.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional THz Spectroscopy of Multiferroic BiFeO3
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Multiferroic materials exhibit coupling between spin, lattice, and electronic degrees of freedom, and the ability to enhance these interactions to drive multiferroic properties may be the key to future high-speed, low-power technologies. We apply two-dimensional (2D) terahertz (THz) spectroscopy to examine these couplings in multiferroic BiFeO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>. With extreme excitation using high-field THz light, 2D THz spectroscopy can reveal how anharmonic phonon-magnon coupling results in coherent energy transfer between modes and can potentially lead to experimental extraction of phonon-magnon coupling constants.

articleTitle: Quadrature Hybrids for Sideband Separating Receivers on the wSMA
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present two quadrature hybrid designs for operation at ~ 345 GHz. These hybrids were designed for sideband separating receivers currently in development for the wideband Submillimeter Array (wSMA). The first design uses a branch-line structure and simulated results show that the image rejection ratio, return loss and isolation are all above 20.6 dB from 280-360 GHz. The second hybrid is a novel design using silicon-mounted cross-guide probes. The simulated results show that the image rejection ratio, return loss and isolation are all above 28.0 dB from 330-360 GHz.

articleTitle: Polarization-Sensitive Fast THz-TDS Scanner in a Portable Form-Factor
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present an upgraded handheld THz-TDS polarimetric scanner for use in clinical settings and nondestructive testing applications. We have converted an ASOPS system to perform ECOPS time-domain data acquisition to improve measurement rate to about 800 Hz, resulting in TDS measurement time of 1.25 ms. Moreover, the addition of a second detection channel allows co- and cross-polarization elements of the reflected beam to be measured. We present polarization-sensitive imaging results from partial thickness in vivo porcine burns.

articleTitle: Unveiling the ultrafast optoelectronic properties of 3D Dirac semi-metal Cd3As2
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We employ ultrafast optical-pump terahertz-probe spectroscopy and ultrafast THz emission spectroscopy to investigate the ultrafast charge carrier dynamics in the 3D Dirac semi-metal Cd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>As<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>. We extract the temperature-dependent electron mobility (16,000cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>V<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup> at 5K) for Cd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>As<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> nanowire ensemble. We also demonstrate strong THz emission from both Cd<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>As<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> single crystal and nanowires, whose polarity depends strongly on incident angle and pump polarisation.

articleTitle: The evolving role of Fourier transform spectroscopy in far-infrared space astronomy
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Far-infrared spectroscopic observations of the universe provide a unique means of addressing some of the leading questions in modern astrophysics from the formation of stars and planets in our own galaxy to the evolution of galaxies over cosmic time. The technique of Fourier transform spectroscopy, with its ability to cover a broad spectral range at varying spectral resolution, has played a central role in such observations. The history of Fourier transform spectroscopy is reviewed and the evolving role of this technique in the era of photon counting infrared detectors discussed.

articleTitle: Energy levels and THz optical properties in Graphene Quantum Dots
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Owing to their energy level splitting in the meV range, large graphene quantum dots (size ~100 nm) are very attractive candidates for THz technology. Whereas their electronic properties have been widely studied by transport measurements, only very few works have been focused on their interaction with THz radiation. Here, we report a theoretical and experimental investigation of the optical properties at THz frequencies of large graphene quantum dots. Using a tight-binding modeling, we show the existence of spatially extended mixed-states that should couple efficiently to THz photons. Furthermore, we experimentally demonstrate THz optical absorption of an array of circular 75 nm-diameter graphene quantum dots at 4K and 300K.

articleTitle: Theoretical study of quantum-correlated optical-terahertz biphotons
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We study the statistical properties of optical-terahertz biphotons generated by means of spontaneous parametric down conversion. Numerical dependence of the second-order correlation function is obtained depending on polar angular aperture.

articleTitle: Preliminary Cold Test of a Terahertz Band Sheet Beam Travelling Wave Tube
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this paper, the preliminary cold test of a high frequency system composed of two identical input / output couplers and a 90-period double-staggered grating waveguide is presented. A HFS without dielectric attenuators was machined by nano-CNC machining. The vector network analyzer measured results showed that the transmission coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{21}$</tex> and port reflection <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{11}$</tex> were better than −8.0 dB and −15.0 dB in the bandwidth of ∼47.2 GHz (241.4-288.6 GHz), respectively. The measured results were indicative of satisfactory machining accuracy and surface roughness and verified the adopted manufacturing technique.

articleTitle: Comparison of Optoelectronic Time- and Frequency-Domain Systems for Single- and Multilayer Thickness Measurements
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present the first comparison of optoelectronic frequency- and time-domain terahertz (THz) systems for thickness measurements on sub-mm single- and multilayer samples using identical setups, samples and evaluation procedures in order to obtain comparable results. We find that single layer PET and Kapton foils with a thickness of 23 μm - 350 μm can be measured with similar accuracy with both systems. Hence, frequency-domain THz systems may replace time-domain systems in future industrial layer thickness measurements.

articleTitle: Evaluation for GaN single crystals with high doping concentration by the terahertz ellipsometry
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Gallium nitride (GaN) single crystals with high carrier concentration up to 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup> order were evaluated by the terahertz time-domain spectroscopic ellipsometry. The electric properties such as carrier density are obtained by the fitting analysis based on Drude model. The terahertz ellipsometry is powerful non-contact and non-destructive evaluation method for semiconductors with high carrier concentration.

articleTitle: Fine structure of excitonic excited states in diamond studied by broadband terahertz time-domain spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Diamond provides a unique excitonic fine structure not seen in conventional semiconductors. Here, we have applied deep-ultraviolet pump and broadband terahertz probe spectroscopy to investigate internal transitions of excitons in intrinsic diamond. Transient absorption spectra clearly show a fine structure splitting in the 2P state of the exciton, that comes from the spin-orbit interaction and the mass anisotropy of electrons and holes. Splitting energies and relative oscillator strengths are reproduced well by the theoretical model.

articleTitle: Characterization of Kapton, FeBO3 and sapphire in the THz region
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We measure Kapton, FeBO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and sapphire in the terahertz region with a time-domain spectrometer and fit the measurement with Lorentz and Debye oscillators as well as scattering to extract the refractive index and absorption under 5 THz.

articleTitle: THz Technique in Confirming Pharmacological Rules of Thumb
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The attenuated total reflection (ATR) technique of spectroscopy in combination with the terahertz technique (THz) is being investigated to find rotatable bonds, which are considered to be one of the rules of thumb given by Veber et al.

articleTitle: Terahertz nano-spectroscopy with resonant scattering probes
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We propose and demonstrate tunable resonant scattering probes for terahertz (THz) near-field microscopy, using sharp indium tips fabricated to the tine of a quartz tuning fork. We find the antenna resonance of the indium tips can be tuned by altering the tip length, which we support with numerical models. We also demonstrate the indium tips can provide nanoscale field confinement at the tip apex, with spatial resolution better than 100 nm.

articleTitle: Extreme Terahertz-wave Parametric oscillator and its application
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This paper presents examination of a backward Terahertz-wave (THz-wave) parametric oscillator (BW - TPO) with wide tunability in the sub-THz wave region (~1 THz). The simple and compact device has been demonstrated under a special optical parametric down-conversion found in a periodically poled lithium niobate. The potential property of the BW - TPO is expected to pave the way for THz-wave applications, especially a swept-source THz OCT with a higher depth-resolution because of a dynamically wide frequency-tuning range.

articleTitle: An ADAM Optimization for Water-Vapor Effect Removal in THz-TDS Data
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: An ADAM optimization method, implemented using the Theano framework, for water-vapor effect removal from THz-TDS (terahertz time-domain spectroscopy) data is proposed. The cost function is derived from the ratio between the energy in the main THz pulse and the oscillation after the pulse as in [1]. A quantitative experimental validation of the method is performed. For free space measurement, the cost function is 0.018 in a sealed N2 environment, 0.043 in an open environment and 0.020 for the open environment data after applying the method. In addition, a qualitative improvement of D-(-)-Quinic acid's THz absorbance measurement in an open environment, where atmospheric humidity exists, is demonstrated. The cross-correlation between the D-(-)-Quinic acid's absorbance spectrum measured in a sealed N2 environment and one measured in an open environment increases from 0.044 to 0.62 after the water-vapor effect removal method is applied.

articleTitle: Identification, Assignment, and Characterization of Low-Frequency Dynamics in Microplastic Pollutants
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: As single-use plastics have become more widely used, the proper disposal of such products becomes increasingly critical. Unfortunately, these materials have not traditionally been properly disposed of, and have polluted the environment from rivers to oceans. In order to study and combat the tolls this has taken on the environment, the broken-down plastics, known as microplastics, must be identified and characterized, which can be done through vibrational spectroscopy. Low-frequency vibrational spectra provide insights into the bulk and molecular structures, and is a promising tool for microplastic characterization.

articleTitle: Caught in the act: Excited-state Proton Transfer to the solvent followed in real time by non-linear THz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have investigated the solvent response after photoexcitation using Optical Pump THz Probe (OPTP) spectroscopy with sub-ps time resolution in combination with quantum-chemical modeling. Excited State Proton Transfer (ESPT) is found to be facilitated by excitation of an intermolecular stretch (H<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pyranine</sub>-O<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">water</sub>) triggered by an instantaneous (<; 100 fs) redistribution of charge density. Initiation of proton transfer is observed on a time scale of 0.4 ps, i.e. on a much shorter time scale than anticipated before. Our results demonstrate the exceptional sensitivity of OPTP, which enables us to follow the proton motion into the hydrogen bond network of water exploring charge transport in transient solvent configurations in real time.

articleTitle: Bi-aspheric singlet THz lenses free of spherical aberration
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present fabricated bi-aspheric singlet lenses, free of spherical aberrations. The lenses are made from cyclic olefin copolymer Topas material and fabricated using Computer Numerical Control (CNC) lathe machining.

articleTitle: Investigation on Dual Frequency Operation in Double Confocal Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Double confocal cavity shows good performance in high efficiency harmonic gyrotron development. Due to its specific configuration, dual frequency operation in double confocal gyrotron which has two different pairs of confocal mirrors is proposed. In this paper, the attempting of dual frequency operation in double confocal gyrotron is investigated by particle-in-cell simulation. A TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,8</sub> fundamental and TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,15</sub> second harmonic double confocal cavity is designed. In particle-in-cell simulation, both fundamental and second harmonic modes are stimulated simultaneously. The maximum 2.6 kW output power is observed, in which the power of fundamental TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,8</sub> mode is 2 kW, and the power of second harmonic TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0,15</sub> mode is 0.6 kW. The results demonstrate that it is capable to generate dual frequency output at different harmonics by double confocal gyrotron.

articleTitle: Investigation of two-dimensional plasmons in grating-gated AlGaN/GaN heterostructures with terahertz time domain spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) plasmons in grating-gated AlGaN/GaN heterostructures were investigated by terahertz time domain spectroscopy observing the distinctive minima and inflection points in the transmission amplitude and phase spectra, respectively. The main features of 2D plasmons at temperature of 80 K were the fundamental mode position at 2.2 THz (grating period of 600 nm, filling 50%), the quality factor up to 8 and the modulation of transmission amplitude and phase up to 50% and 18 deg, respectively (period 1000 nm, filling 80%).

articleTitle: Longitudinal Optical Phonon Resonant THz – Mid Infrared Radiation From Surface Metal-Semiconductor Microstructures
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: THz-mid infrared electric-dipole radiation resonating with longitudinal optical (LO) phonon energy is obtained from metal-semiconductor surface microstructures by heating samples for various types of semiconductors. The structures using undoped GaAs yield emission peaked at 8.5 THz. The emission properties depending on structural parameters are consistent to the electric dipole properties. The emission from n<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>-GaP resonates with the LO phonon, which indicates the feasibility of THz emission by optical excitation using indirect electronic transition type materials. The emission from undoped and p-type doped Ga<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sub>In<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5</sub>P presents two peaks, which indicates the feasibility of electromagnetically induced transparency at an emission energy toward optical gain.

articleTitle: Layer-thickness measurements with incoherent terahertz light
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We recently demonstrated the use of incoherent light from a superluminescent diode to drive a terahertz crosscorrelation spectroscopy system. Its application to layer-thickness measurement tasks is the scope of this contribution. The limitations and a comparison to layer-thickness measurements with a standard time-domain spectroscopy system is discussed with a special focus of the bandwidth-dependence of the layer-thickness evaluation result.

articleTitle: Pulsed THz emission from wurtzite phase catalyst-free InAs nanowires
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The wurtzite phase catalyst-free InAs nanowires were investigated under femtosecond optical pulse photoexcitations. It was found that the THz radiation emission mechanisms depend on an exciting laser beam polarization, namely, the plasma oscillations for perpendicular to nanowire optical electric fields, and the ballistically moving carrier separation for the parallel polarization fields. The energetic distance between Γ7c and Γ8c conduction bands was experimentally determined to be 0.5 eV.

articleTitle: Probing of Oleic Acid Capped CdSe Quantum Dot Surface Using Visible-Infrared Sum Frequency Generation Spectroscopy: Polarization Dependence, Coupling Effects and Orientational Analysis
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Polarization dependence and orientational analysis studies on surface of QDs are carried out as original work here. Selective enhancement of CH3 stretching vibration modes is observed at resonance wavelengths based on coupling effects.

articleTitle: Development of a 28 GHz 50kW CW Gyrotron for ECRH application
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A 28GHz 50kW gyrotron has been developed for ECRH application in plasma fusion system. The gyrotron employed a triode magnetron injection gun, a cylindrical cavity working under a TE02 mode, a built-in quasi-optical mode converter with ~92% conversion efficiency, and a single-stage depressed collector. In the test, a Gaussian beam of 55 kW for 30 s continuous wave at 28 GHz has been achieved. The corresponding total efficiency is 46%. Now the gyrotron system has been delivered to the customer site and has been applied in the installation experiment.

articleTitle: Study of development of the electromagnetic wave absorber in terahertz region using metallic microcoil array
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The transmittance properties of the microcoil allay embedded in the epoxy resin were investigated experimentally and calculatedly. The responses of the microcoil array were calculated based on the finite element method. Results show that the microcoil array is an effective electromagnetic wave absorber in the sub-terahertz region.

articleTitle: Terahertz quantum sensing with visible light
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In quantum sensing experiments, photons in the spectral region of interest interact with a sample and their properties are transferred via biphoton-correlation to another spectral region, where widely available and highly developed detectors can be used. Especially spectral regions where the photon detection is quite difficult can benefit from this novel technique. We report on the first demonstration of quantum sensing in the terahertz frequency range, in which the terahertz photons interact with a sample in free space determining the thickness of polytetrafluoroethylene plates by only detecting visible photons [1].

articleTitle: High speed mid-IR Quantum Cascade Detector at room temperature
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a high-speed antenna enhanced Quantum Cascade Detector at 10.3μm. By using a coherent detection scheme and thin InGaAs/AlInAs heterostructure embedded in metal-metal patch antenna, we demonstrate a heterodyne response up to 67 GHz at room temperature.

articleTitle: Achievements and challenges for ITER heating & current drive systems
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The ITER project is a major step in the development of fusion energy aiming to demonstrate the feasibility of exploiting magnetic confinement fusion for the production of energy in an experiment close to the dimensions of a future commercial fusion reactor. To achieve high fusion gain and control several aspects of the plasma behavior, three heating systems capable of injecting a total power up to 73 MW will be installed. This paper will summarize the requirements of the three systems and will highlight the main achievements in their design and construction.

articleTitle: Hyperspectral 2D IR imaging: Principles and applications to biological and materials systems
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This talk intends to give an insight into 2D IR spectroscopy, a powerful tool for studying protein folding and aggregation, liquid structure, and the dynamics of small molecules. In 2D IR, infrared spectra are spread into a second dimension, providing information on vibrational couplings, and separating the effects of homogeneous and inhomogeneous dynamics. It provides information about molecular structures and dynamics through cross-peaks and 2D lineshapes, respectively. There has been a recent push to turn this spectroscopy into hyperspectral microscopy. With hyperspectral 2D IR imaging, vibrational couplings, 2D lineshapes, and non-linear signals can be imaged, providing insights into spatial heterogeneity.

articleTitle: Study of harmonic generation from InSb excited by terahertz wave pulses with femtosecond pulse laser excitation
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The excited density dependences for InSb by intense terahertz pulses whose central frequency is 0.5 THz with femtosecond pulse laser excitation were investigated in detail. The transmitted terahertz waveforms with perpendicular polarization to incident beam change drastically at the low- and high-density excitations. The third harmonic generation around 1.5 THz is observed.

articleTitle: Numerical Study on Injection Locking in Resonant Tunneling Diode Oscillators
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We performed simulations for injection locking of a submillimeter-wave RTD oscillator circuit. A wider locking range is realized with optimizing the position where the injection signal is applied.

articleTitle: Colossal Terahertz Field Enhancement in Slant Nano-Antennas
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Metallic nanostructures have important roles in electromagnetic field manipulations due to the localization of electromagnetic waves, for which fabrication techniques in nanotechnology have been developed. To achieve higher field enhancement, it is required to decrease the dimensions of the nanostructures such as thickness or width of the gap. Here, we fabricated the slant nano-antennas where a portion of metals on each side is overlapped. The slant nano-antennas realize higher electromagnetic field enhancement while keeping background noise almost zero.

articleTitle: A 63-Pixel Terahertz Focal-Plane Array for Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy and Imaging
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a high-sensitivity and broadband photoconductive terahertz focal-plane array with 63 pixels. We utilize a plasmonic nanoantenna array and an optical diffuser to provide a high spatial overlap between the received terahertz field and the optical pump beam to offer an efficient terahertz detection performance. We experimentally demonstrate more than a 60 dB signal-to-noise ratio and a 2 THz detection bandwidth for all of the pixels of the focal-plane array.

articleTitle: An investigation of THz label-free opioid sensing
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present numerical modeling and experiments on the THz electromagnetic signatures of various opioid powders.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency Terahertz Raman Spectra of Graphite Flakes and Single-Walled Carbon Nanotube Aerogel
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We investigate THz Raman spectra of graphite flakes and SWCNT aerogel in an ambient environment using 532 nm laser excitation. a number of spectral features were obtained between 20 and 300 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>. the layer breathing mode and ZO' mode, together with their combination modes, are prominent in graphite flakes spectrum. the main feature of the SWCNT spectrum are radial breathing modes for SWCNT's of different diameter.

articleTitle: High Q factor and high transmittance suspended membrane THz PhC cavity: experimental demonstration for sensing applications
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present designs and measurements of integrated high resistivity (HR) Si PhC waveguide Bragg reflectors with 100 GHz band gap close to 0.6THz, respectively suspended in air or supported by a teflon tube. Resonant defect modes both in the air and dielectric Bloch bands of the PhC with large Q factors (up to 18000) and high transmittance (up to 72%) are measured and reported by engineering the periodicity of the PhC mirrors.

articleTitle: Monte Carlo Simulations of ultrafast nonlinear THz optical properties in n-doped In0.53Ga0.47As
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We investigate the nonlinear optical effects induced by incident THz fields, varying its energy and width; leading to a transmission enhancement effect in doped semiconductors due to strong intervalley scattering, over the picosecond time scales. Besides that, we observed higher harmonics generation in the shortest pulse than in the larger ones. However, the THz transmission enhancement increased with the pulse's width.

articleTitle: Terahertz quantum cascade laser frequency comb operation of a coupled waveguide array
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We present a terahertz quantum cascade laser array of laterally coupled waveguides with varying length. At a relatively low bias, a regular mode spacing and a single beatnote are observed, which are signatures of frequency comb operation. The comb spectrum spans 650 GHz and consists of groups of modes separated by a multiple of the mode spacing, indicating that the waveguides combine to form a global comb.

articleTitle: Doubly Resonant Internally Heterodyne Phase Resolved Vibrational Sum Frequency Generation spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Advancements in sum frequency generation spectroscopy have expanded its versatility in recent years. Despite this little investigation into the synergistic combination of advanced approaches has been reported. Here we combined the signal enhancing doubly resonant excitation scheme, which probes the vibronic structure of the sample, with the phase resolving capabilities of internally heterodyne phase resolved detection. Ultimately this combination of technique demonstrates the influence that the electronic transition involved in doubly resonant sum frequency generation has on the surface susceptibility, in tandem with acquisition of the chemical and electronic sample dependent response.

articleTitle: Excited state dynamics of conducting polymers studied by time-resolved optical and terahertz spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Terahertz time-domain, optical pump-THz probe and optical pump-optical probe spectroscopies are used to study the optoelectronic properties of two PEDOT-based conducting polymers: PEDOT/PSTFSIK and PEDOT/PSS. These experiments highlight the role played by polarons and bipolarons in the carriers' dynamics taking place within these compounds after their photoexcitation by ultrashort optical pulses.

articleTitle: Effect of substrate material on LT-GaAs carrier dynamics at 800 nm
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Carrier dynamics of two LT-GaAs layers grown using similar parameters, but on different substrates were studied. The behavior of the time-resolved terahertz transmission was observed to differ in trapping time constants, as well as in fluence-dependence. The differences are attributed to the difference in layer quality when using different substrates, wherein the use of silicon substrates result in increased structural defect density in the silicon substrate-grown layer, which provide additional scattering and non-recombination pathways, resulting in the reduced carrier lifetime.

articleTitle: Notice of Retraction: Ponderomotive Force Analysis of Terahertz Generation in Liquid Water
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Retracted.

articleTitle: 3D Aperture in THz Bull's Eye Structure for Sub-Wavelength Resolution Sensing
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report a study on three-dimensional transmission aperture of terahertz (THz) Bull's Eye structure. By applying three-dimensional aperture to a Bull's Eye structure, it is possible to achieve a higher intensity of electric field and localization of electric field distribution than a conventional Bull's Eye structure having two-dimensional aperture. In addition, it can also be utilized in measurement when the sample surface has roughness, which is useful in sensing and imaging applications.

articleTitle: Observing liquid water build-up in proton exchange membrane fuel cells using terahertz imaging and high-resolution optical gauging
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The performance and durability of proton exchange membrane fuel cells are closely linked to effective water management strategies. Inadequate water balance results in polymer electrolyte membrane (PEM) dehydration or water flooding, both leading to performance loss and possible cell failure. Exploiting the contrast from liquid water absorption and transparency of dielectric materials, such as polymers, at terahertz (THz) frequencies, we apply a simple, compact THz imaging system to image water build-up in the flow channels of a THz-transparent fuel cell supported by high resolution optical gauging.

articleTitle: THz Nonlinear Dielectrics
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We experimentally investigate the dielectric response of two different liquid samples through nonlinear terahertz spectroscopy. Our results indicate that the nonlinear indexes of refraction of these liquids in the terahertz frequency range are up to six orders higher than those in the optical regime with an averaged value of 7.8±3×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-10</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/W for water and 1.30 ± 0.01×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-10</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/W for α-pinene.

articleTitle: Dual-Field Superfocusing Based on Near-field Metasurfaces
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work, a terahertz near-field metasurface is proposed to superfocus both electric and magnetic fields. To achieve a sharp dual-field superfocusing, a sort of minuscule unit cell is designed to elaborately arrange the array accordingly. The full widths at half-maximum (FWHMs) of the electric and magnetic fields are 0.079λ and 0.052λ at a distance of 0.1λ. The proposed dual-field superfocusing holds potential benefits for multiple-target sensing, extreme subwavelength lithography, super-resolution imaging, and data storage and access.

articleTitle: Development of a Broadband Multidimensional THz Spectrometer
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this work we discuss the development of a multidimensional terahertz (THz) spectrometer, incorporating a range of THz generation and detection schemes in order to improve the flexibility and practicality of these complex experimental setups.

articleTitle: Probing the Low-Temperature Phase Transition in $\text{Er}_{x}\mathrm{Y}_{1-x}\text{FeO}_{3}$ by Terahertz Magnetospectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We have studied the terahertz response of the rare-earth orthoferrite Er<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sub>Y<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</sub>FeO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> as a function of magnetic field, temperature, and yttrium composition ( x). Through theoretical modelling based on an extended Dicke Hamiltonian, we provide new insight into the role of cooperative, “superradiant” interactions between Er spins and Fe magnons in the low-temperature phase transition that this magnetic system exhibits.

articleTitle: Towards high quality 3D printed THz devices with cyclic olefin polymer
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: There is an urgent need for low cost and easily accessible optical devices for THz applications. New optical devices can be manufactured rapidly with 3D printing while using THz transparent materials. In this work, to 3D print high-quality THz waveguides, we optimized the parameters for high-resolution 3D printing of a THz transparent filament, cyclic olefin copolymer.

articleTitle: Super-resolution Terahertz Microscopy with Deterministic Artificial Fluorophores
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We develop a super-resolution terahertz imaging technique to improve the THz image resolution beyond the diffraction limit. Inspired by super-resolution techniques developed in the visible range, we design artificial fluorophores that blink deterministically to reconstruct images of higher resolution using as little as 8 frames.

articleTitle: Electrically-Driven THz-wave Demodulation with a Photomixer : Theory and Experiment
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Phase-sensitive demodulation of the signal from a modulated THz-wave is theoretically and experimentally demonstrated by using the detection with a low-temperature grown GaAs photomixer that is electrically-driven with an alternative voltage at the modulation frequency.

articleTitle: Continuous Wave Sub-Terahertz Lensless Holographic Reflective Imaging
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We propose a simple setup involving standard commercially available sub-terahertz electronic source and camera in reflection layout. The setup is designed for imaging amplitude and phase objects. The construction allows for quick installation and potentially almost-realtime operation. Initial reconstruction results demonstrate resolution of about three wavelengths.

articleTitle: Total internal reflection geometry for near-field imaging
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The often unique responses of everyday materials to mm-wave and THz radiation mean that imaging at these frequencies is of great interest in research and industry alike. To this end, we have designed and demonstrated a single-pixel near-field mm-wave imaging system that is capable of resolving subwavelength features in biological tissues in a few seconds.

articleTitle: Taming Extraordinary THz Transmission through Sub-$\lambda$ Slot Arrays via Array Truncation, Slot Rotation, Polarization and Angle of Incidence
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Accurate and time-effective simulation and design optimization of quasi-optical (QO) systems is an extremely challenging electromagnetic problem given the multi-scale dimension of QO components and the need to consider the finite size of such components to account for effects like diffraction. To show that the Method of Moments (MoM) provides an elegant solution for these problems, truncated rectangular arrays of tilted slots are measured in a QO Terahertz (THz) time-domain setup and comparison with MoM is carried out. The extraordinary transmission peaks are modulated by the size of the array and the orientation of the slots with respect to the incident electric field.

articleTitle: Terahertz Driven Ultrafast Electron Sources
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We review progress towards the attempt to build THz driven and THz aided ultrafast electron sources suitable for ultrafast electron diffraction and injection of follow on THz accelerator systems that may later drive X-ray sources. Sources are based on either single-cycle or multi-cycle THz radiation. Where possible, we relate designs to already achieved experimental results as well as to the available THz sources for different pulse formats.

articleTitle: Photon-assisted tunneling in hBN encapsulated graphene quantum dot under coherent THz illumination
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: We report photon-assisted tunneling in a hBN encapsulated graphene quantum dot under coherent THz illumination. We demonstrate transport assisted by THz photons within the Coulomb blockade regime. We study the dependence on frequencies and intensity of satellite currents generated by THz illumination. Our study opens promising perspectives for the development of quantum devices and for probing light-matter interaction phenomena.

articleTitle: 550 GHz Scanning Lens Phased Array
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: In this contribution, we present the progress towards developing two submillimeter-wave prototypes of a scanning lens phased array. This recently-proposed array architecture can achieve high-gain, wide-scan radiation patterns with low sidelobes and only a few active elements. Measurements are presented for a prototype lens antenna at 550 GHz.

articleTitle: Completely Passive Room-Temperature Imaging of Human Body Radiation Below 1 THz with Field-Effect Transistors
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: This work presents to our knowledge the first completely passive imaging of human body radiation below 1 THz at the room temperature without additional illumination or cooling. The successful image shows an impressive sensitivity limit of a terahertz FET detector (TeraFET). We made a 2.7 cm × 4 cm size image of a hand with the spatial resolution of 1 mm and scanning speed equal to 1 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/100 s. The SNR is only 2.5 dB and the NETD of the hand radiation at room temperature is 4.8 K.

articleTitle: Controlling and shaping the THz emission from Quantum Cascade Lasers
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: The control of the output beam shape and direction of THz Quantum Cascade Lasers is presented. For the improvement of the operation temperature different barrier heights are investigated. As result a very efficient device is realized which requires only thermo-electric cooling and thus can be integrated into compact gas spectroscopy systems.

articleTitle: Theoretical Study on the Possibility for Stepwise Tuning of the Frequency of the KIT 2 MW 170/204 GHz Coaxial-Cavity Gyrotron
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: A first theoretical study on the possibility for stepwise frequency tuning of a dual-frequency 170/204 GHz TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">34,19</sub>/TE<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">40,23</sub>-mode coaxial-cavity gyortron pre-prototype, under development at KIT, has been done. A bandwidth of ± 10 GHz around both center frequencies has been considered as tuning range. For each of the two bands, in total 11 modes have been selected to cover the entire frequency range. The theoretical study has shown that just changing the azimuthal index of the operating mode to obtain an appropriate mode series for frequency step-tunability is insufficient because the insert loading constraint is not fulfilled. A new mode series has been found, where the insert loading constraint is obeyed.

articleTitle: Anisotropic Charge Conduction in Oriented Donor-Acceptor Polymer Films and Liquid Dispersions Measured by Time-Resolved Terahertz Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2020 45th International Conference on Infrared, Millimeter, and Terahertz Waves (IRMMW-THz)
abstract: Time-Resolved Terahertz methods with polarized pump-probe analysis are employed to extract conduction and mobility anisotropy of conjugated donor-acceptor polymers as films and liquid dispersions.
